summary: Coachmarks in a sequence — one at a time, each pointing at its target, with "2 of 4", Back, Next, and Done on the last. Steps are data, naming their targets by id; a target not on the page is skipped.
useWhen: a first look round a page someone asked to be shown — "Take the tour"
several places matter in an order, and each is best explained beside it
the product wants to know who saw it through: `onComplete` fires for Done only

useInstead.when: one place, one thing to say
useInstead.why: a tour of one has no count and no Back; a Coachmark says the same with less

useInstead.when: the page itself is new to everyone and needs no pointing — an empty workspace
useInstead.why: an empty page explains itself in place; a tour pointing at nothing yet is five dialogs for one sentence

useInstead.when: telling people something changed without their asking
useInstead.why: a tour takes focus at every step; opened unasked it takes over the page

composition.note: Start it from a button — `isOpen` from its press — and end it through `onOpenChange(false)`. Each step is `{ target: id, title, body, placement? }`. Remember a finished tour in `onComplete`, and offer it again to someone who ended it early. Every string is in `labels`; `progress` receives the current step and the total as numbers.
composition.example: <Tour isOpen={touring} onOpenChange={setTouring} onComplete={markSeen} steps={[{ target: 'overview-range', title: 'Pick the period', body: 'Every figure follows the dates chosen here.' }]} />

requires: start it from a person's action, never on page load: every step takes focus
an `id` on every target, and a `title` on every step — it names that step's dialog
guarantees: one step at a time, each a Coachmark: a non-modal dialog named by its title, focused when it appears so each step is read out
the count, Back and Next / Done sit in each step's footer; there is no Back on the first step, and one step alone has no count
a target not on the page when the tour starts — removed, or not drawn at this width — is skipped, and the count is of the steps that remain
Done on the last step calls `onComplete` and ends the tour; the close button (`labels.close`, "End tour") and Escape end it without completing it
focus goes back to what started the tour once, when it ends, not between steps
started again, it begins at the first step
`onStepChange` receives the step's index in `steps`, so a skipped step never appears in it
notes: The page is measured once, when the tour starts: a target that appears mid-tour is not added, so the count never changes under the reader.

antiPatterns.do: a "Take the tour" button, with `seen` deciding only whether to offer it
antiPatterns.why: a tour that opens itself takes focus from whoever arrived to do something else

antiPatterns.dont: steps pointing at elements that exist only after a click in an earlier step
antiPatterns.do: steps over what is on the page when the tour starts
antiPatterns.why: the page is measured when the tour starts; a target that was not there is skipped, and the step with it
Escape on step one is not the same as reading it through; only one of them should stop the offer
